```
Inline comments:
In `@bin/scan-cron.php`:
- Around line 75-117: The script currently prints incidental output during
WP/tenant bootstrap which can corrupt the JSON emitted by the final echo
json_encode($payloads);, so wrap early bootstrap and plugin loading in an output
buffer (start buffering before require_once $wp_load and tenant
switch_to_blog()) and suppress/redirect any buffered output away from stdout
(e.g., send it to stderr or discard) before producing the final payload; ensure
only the JSON produced from iterating _get_cron_array() and
Job_Payload::from_cron_event(...) is written to stdout by flushing/cleaning the
buffer and then calling echo json_encode($payloads).

In `@src/class-job-payload.php`:
- Around line 114-131: current_site_id() currently trusts domain_index alone and
falls back to get_current_blog_id(), which diverges from the validation used in
bin/execute-job.php and bin/scan-cron.php (they validate sites[$site_id],
isolation_model === 'sovereign', and domain membership), so update
current_site_id() to reuse the same validation contract: extract the
sovereign-tenant check into a shared helper (e.g., is_sovereign_site($site_id,
$host) or validate_sovereign_site_from_registry) and call that helper from
current_site_id() instead of directly trusting domain_index or falling back to
get_current_blog_id(); ensure the helper enforces sites[$site_id] exists,
isolation_model === 'sovereign', and that $host is a member of that site before
returning the $site_id, and keep honoring WU_MT_SOVEREIGN_TENANT when defined.

In `@src/class-worker-process.php`:
- Around line 371-377: The current check uses sovereign_site_entries() (which
only returns active entries with domains) to skip switch_to_blog, so sovereign
tenants with incomplete registry metadata still fall through; change the logic
to build two separate sets: (1) a sovereign_ids skip-list containing all
sovereign tenant IDs (derive from the registry/sovereign source or by extracting
IDs from sovereign_site_entries() plus any additional registry lookup) and (2)
the existing runnable_sovereign_entries (the current sovereign_site_entries()
result) used for subprocess scanning; then replace the current if
(isset($sovereign_sites[$site_id])) continue; with a check against sovereign_ids
to always skip switch_to_blog($site_id), while preserving the runnable entries
logic for the scan; apply the same two-list split and skip-by-ID fix in the
other block handling sites (the code around the second occurrence referenced).
- Around line 485-520: rescan_sovereign_site_jobs() currently blocks the
Workerman event loop by calling proc_open() then synchronously reading
stdout/stderr with stream_get_contents() and proc_close(); change it to spawn
the subprocess non-blockingly and integrate it with the existing async process
handling (the same mechanism used by the batch path and poll_processes()), or at
minimum set pipes non-blocking (stream_set_blocking(..., false)), read
incrementally (stream_select or event-driven reads) and enforce a hard timeout
that calls proc_terminate() and proc_close() on expiry. Locate
rescan_sovereign_site_jobs, the callsites in rescan_all_jobs/on_worker_start and
Timer::add, and the poll_processes logic to either register the new process with
the same async tracker or implement non-blocking reads + timeout so the worker
timers and socket handling are not stalled.
```

</details>
